table_metadata.table_purpose: Schedule for participants who continue ramucirumab treatment in the continued-access period, plus its own follow-up visit.
table_metadata.notes: track, not domain or continuation: the column structure is entirely different from Table 1 (two columns, visits 501-5XX and 901) and it schedules a different study phase - participants who have moved into the continued-access period - rather than a different activity category on Table 1's timeline. track_label taken from the table's own title. 1 leading label column, so data columns are 2-3; column 4 is a right-hand Instructions notes column and carries no schedule data.

schedule_properties.property_comment: Top header row naming the two phases of the continued-access period: 'Study Treatment' and 'Follow-Up'. Phase names -> epoch. The label cell of column 1 is vertically merged across header rows 1-2 and its text ('Visit') sits on the row-2 line, so this row's name is synthesized.
Visit-number row: '501-5XX' for the continued-access treatment visits and '901' for the follow-up visit. Visit identifiers -> visit.

annotations.annotation_text: Continued-access follow-up begins when the participant and the investigator agree that the participant will no longer continue treatment in the continued-access period and lasts a minimum of 30 days following the last dose of study drug.  In all cases, no follow-up procedures will be performed for a participant who withdraws informed consent unless he or she has explicitly provided permission and consent.

annotations.annotation_text: Grading via CTCAE, Version 5.0.  As part of AE collection, monitor vital signs and perform standard laboratory tests (hematology, chemistry, urinalysis, and pregnancy testing) at the same frequency as during the study treatment period.  See Section 10.3 for AE grading for lab investigations.  All laboratory tests during the continued access period will be performed in the local laboratories only.

annotations.annotation_text: In the event of hypersensitivity, blood samples will be collected for PK, IG, and exploratory hypersensitivity analyses at the following time points, as close as possible to:  (i) the onset of the hypersensitivity, (ii) the resolution of the hypersensitivity, and (iii) 30 (±3) days following the hypersensitivity.
